what_it_does: Cloud providers store data on large banks of physical disk servers (called storage warehouses), and they must decide which virtual disks to place on which physical servers — a problem called placement. Current placement algorithms treat storage load as static, but real workloads fluctuate over time: a server that looks lightly loaded right now may become a hot spot tonight when backup jobs run. Tela addresses this by modeling how each storage server's workload varies across different times of day and week, then predicting future load patterns when deciding where to place a new virtual disk. By choosing placements that balance load not just at the moment of placement but also at likely future moments, Tela aims to reduce overloads and improve overall disk server utilization in large cloud deployments.
